lines.en: I knock on Io’s door and wait for her to answer.
I’m sure I’ll need to knock again or announce my presence at some point to circumnavigate her antisocial tendencies but-
I see no harm in testing the waters each time I arrive.
It’s only a matter of time until that shell of hers crumbles and she winds up greeting anyone who knocks.
If anyone knocks.
There’s no reason anyone would want to at this point, is there?
No one but me, that is.
And it’s not like it’s flattering receiving a visit from me given that my end goal with all of these girls is exactly the same.
To sneak inside of them- in more ways than one.
Into their minds. Into their hearts.
Into their sheets.
Their pants.
Their bodies.
And to leave minimal trace behind so my efforts aren’t thwarted somewhere along the line I’m actively trying to erase.
If you think that’s so horrible-
Then just look away.
It’s that easy.
: Io, it’s me.
: Hah...
: Say that after the first knock from now on.
: Come on in, Sensei.
I probably should just say I’m here after the first knock, shouldn’t I?
If my goal is so impure, is the pause to see if she’s grown as a person really all that necessary?
Time is precious.
Or at least it used to be.
But I could still save so much of it by giving up on her.
: Welcome back.
So why won't I do that?
: Hey. Any plans for tonight?
: Not until now.
: Was thinking about taking a trip to the convenience store but my shoes are still soaking wet from walking home in the snow.
: You only have one pair?
: I only need one pair.
: Clearly not if shoes are currently your only barrier from fulfilling your nightly goal.
: Okay, sorry. I usually only need one pair.
: But it’s not like the inability to go on a little walk is something that’s going to ruin my life.
: Especially now that you’re here.
: You’re a little bit more fun than a trek through frozen rain.
: Just a little, though.
: Thanks. I also like you more than I like snow, if that means anything to you.
: It does.
: I have a tendency to think everyone likes everything more than me by default until proven otherwise.
: Well I’m not really in the mood to list all of the things you’re better than, so we should probably just change the topic now.
: Hahah...Probably.
: So, what do you want to do?
: You came all the way here with just your regular blazer on. Aren’t you cold?
: I’d offer you a jacket or something but I’m pretty sure that nothing I have would fit you.
: We can get under the kotatsu if you want?
: It doesn’t turn on since I’m still trying to fix it, but it’s got a blanket and blankets are cool.
: Well, warm. They’re not cool at all. You know what I mean.
: There’s the bed, too.
: Yes. There’s the bed, too.
: If you can reach it, that is.
: You’re gonna have to climb over some stuff to get there so I figured a spot on the floor might be easier for you.
: Are you doubting my agility, Io Ichimonji?
: Woah. Breaking out my last name? You must be really serious right now.
: Never underestimate my willpower to get into bed with a cute girl.
: Ooooh I’ve moved from “bathhouse attendant” to “cute girl” in your book. What a momentous occasion.
: You’ve held both titles since I met you.
: I’m flattered you feel that way, Sensei, but I’m sure it’s just your craving for body heat that is causing you to say such things.
: So I’m sorry but I must reject you. I hope we can stay friends, though.
: And with that, you’ve earned the title of “Uta impressionist” as well.
: Nihihi~ Pretty good, right? I spend so much time with her that it’s basically second nature at this point.
: Come on. We can sit on the bed.
: As long as you can get to it, I mean~
Io manages to slip between a table and a minifridge without bumping into either of them and hops onto her mattress.
I am slightly less successful but still manage to make it through without breaking anything, so this is a victory in my book.
: Congratulations on passing through the barrier.
: I’m impressed you were able to make it through without even touching anything.
: I’m like five feet tall and paperthin. Plus I’ve done it a bunch of times before.
: Muscle memory really helps out with small things like that.
: Also, it’s not weird if I sit this close to you, is it?
: You’re not getting nervous, are you?
: Not at all.
: Are you?
: Not at all.
: I'm just chilling.
: Wanna watch a movie or something? I’ve got a bunch.
: I already told you I’m not into movies.
: Yeah, but I’m obviously gonna try to change your mind when they’re another big hobby of mine.
: You have too many hobbies.
: You don’t have enough hobbies.
: Take something up so we can have a reason to hang out more.
: I was unaware that we needed a reason to hang out more.
: Less of a reason and more of an excuse so that no one will start thinking anything is going on between us.
: If we’re both in like...the golf club or something, nobody will think we’re up to anything if we hang out somewhere after[school].
: At this point, I think it’s pretty safe to assume that anyone and everyone thinks I’m up to something at any given point.
: Being around me probably just opens you up to more pressure like that.
: I don’t care about pressure but...
: Is that really what everyone thinks of you?
: That you’re up to something?
: You’re not, though. Right?
: And even if you were, isn’t it a little obsessive of them to not let you do what you want to do?
: You’re an adult. You don’t have to care about what a bunch of [teenage]girls think. They-
: They’re toxic, yes. I already know how you feel.
: You’ve mentioned it a few times now.
: ...Yeah.
: You know, Sensei...
: I’ve got a lot going on and I’m by no means perfect-
: But I’d never do something like judge you for hanging out with whoever you want to hang out with.
: That’s your prerogative.
: That’s not true and you know it.
: It’s human nature to get jealous of things you don’t have- or things you want.
: It’s clear you want to spend as much time with me as possible, so you’d obviously judge me if I just abandoned you for other girls.
: Yeah, you’re probably right.
: I don’t think I’d ever say anything about it, though.
: That’s because you’re a coward.
: I know.
: And you’re weak.
: Uh-huh...
: And you have stupid hair.
: Okay, now you’re just being mean.
Io moves closer to me and rests her head on my shoulder- something people don’t normally do after you insult them.
Granted, I was just kidding for the most part. But it’s still a strange reaction either way.
: You can keep making fun of me if you want. I don’t mind.
: Sure but-
: This is okay, right? Even though I’m a weak coward with stupid hair?
: There’s nothing cowardly about making a move like this on your teacher.
: You’re right. I’m actually kind of awesome, aren’t I?
: You’re definitely unique, if not anything else.
: That’s far from a compliment, Sensei.
: Being unique can be a death sentence sometimes.
: Also, you don’t actually think my hair is stupid, do you?
: It’s like, one of the three things I like about myself.
: What are the other two?
: My eyes and how I can still get out of bed in the morning.
: That last one is a little more real than I was expecting, but I get it.
: Do you have three things you like about yourself, Sensei?
: I’m not even sure I have one.
: And you call me a coward. That’s the most cowardly thing I’ve ever heard.
: Everyone has something they like about themselves. Even if it’s something small like how you look in a particular photo or how your voice sounds when you sing in the shower.
: There’s gotta be something in there.
: I’ve already found plenty of stuff I like about you.
: Name one.
: Your shoulder’s really comfortable. And warm.
: And I like how you still come talk to me despite me being overbearing and annoyingly sensitive.
: Yeah. You’re kind of hard to talk to at times.
: True. But at least I'm more interesting than the rest of the girls in class, right?
: I mean, why else would you be here tonight instead of with any of them?
: Not to mention, I haven’t even seen you with that one blonde girl again since the two of you showed up at the bathhouse.
: Are you bored of her now that you have me?
: I’ve gotta say, I kind of get it.
: She seemed a little too plain anyway.
: Pretty, but plain.
: Obviously, I’m sure there’s a lot more to it than that.
: But even the fact that you’re letting me rest my head on your shoulder like this-
: What are you doing?
: Hm?
: What do you mean?
: Aren’t we bonding?
: Did I say something wrong?
: This is your idea of bonding?
: Talking down about people you’ve never even spoken with?
: That blonde girl's name is Ayane and she’s far from plain.
: She’s actually one of the most unique people I’ve ever met.
: Wait, I wasn’t trying to talk down on her. I was just...
: Just what?
: I...I was just trying to make you think I was...more interesting.
: There are ways to do that without making everyone else seem small.
: You’re underestimating how much you’ve impressed me so far.
: Don’t ruin all of that by belittling people you know nothing about.
The caterpillar squirms once more.
: I’m sorry.
: There’s no sense in apologizing to me.
: Just think more about what you’re saying before you actually say it.
: You’re smart. Bad with people, maybe, but really...really smart.
: Sensei...
: You’re better than this. That’s all I’m saying.
: Well...
: Why are you here, then?
: If there are other interesting people who don’t do things like talk down on everyone around them, why come here?
: I just...thought there was a reason for it. That’s all.
: I’m here because I wanted to be here.
: Don’t overthink it or try to turn it into some sort of equation that needs to be solved.
: Not everything happens for a reason. Sometimes things just...happen.
: Sometimes...things just happen...
: I messed up big time, didn’t I?
: Yeah.
: But you’re still learning.
: Just don’t be a bitch and everything will work out fine.
: I like the head patting thing but not so much the being called a bitch part.
: I guess I deserve it, though.
: Either way, please don’t stop. That feels really nice.
I leave my hand on Io’s head for reasons beyond my comprehension...but I feel like a good portion of them are simply due to how cute she is.
Frankly, though...I’m actually kind of mad right now.
It’s one thing to not associate with any of the other girls- a thing I can understand and respect.
But to do something like demean them behind their backs without even attempting to understand where they come from-
Isn’t that exactly why Io dislikes girls in the first place?
Because they start unnecessary drama?
Is she really this desperate for affection?
Or is it something else?
Something I don’t understand yet.
I don’t stay much longer after that, but not because I don’t want to.
Io actually asks me to leave so she can get a head start on some new thing she wants to build.
I try asking what she plans on making, but she hurries me out of the room in suspiciously quick fashion.
It is what it is, though.
I’m not interested in dampening her creative process when she seems weirdly motivated all of a sudden.
I just hope that whatever it is she makes doesn’t wind up collecting dust on her shelf for the rest of eternity.
Io’s affection has increased to [io_love]!
